model_annotation:
The pie chart presents survey results on the perceived level of integration of design in product development processes within an organization. There are five sectors in the chart, each represented by a different color. The sectors are labeled as follows: "Very integrated" (blue), "Fairly integrated" (orange), "Good integration" (green), "Poorly integrated" (red), and "Not integrated at all" (purple). 

The size of the sector labeled "Fairly integrated" is the largest, indicating that 24% of respondents believe that design is fairly integrated in the product development process. The sector labeled "Good integration" is the second largest, representing 25% of respondents. The sector labeled "Very integrated" is smaller, representing 10% of respondents. The sector labeled "Poorly integrated" is even smaller, representing 8% of respondents. The sector labeled "Not integrated at all" is the smallest, representing 20% of respondents.

In summary, the majority of respondents feel that design is either fairly or good integrated in the product development process, but a significant minority believes it is poorly integrated or not integrated at all.
